cats.words: What we say, and never say

q.q: What is a Delta One module?
o: A purchase of the AI trading engine, as software, for an amount the member chooses
A loan to the trading desk
q.w: A module is a purchase of the Delta One AI trading engine â€” software as a service â€” for the amount the member chooses. It is never a deposit, an investment or a share.

q.q: What is the minimum purchase for a module?
q.w: Modules start at 1,000 USDT; any amount above is allowed.

q.q: In which currency and on which network is a module paid?
q.w: USDT on BNB Smart Chain (BEP-20). Results and commissions are paid the same way.

q.q: What is the most a module can ever deliver?
o: 2Ã— its purchase price, price included â€” then it ends
Unlimited, as long as it runs
q.w: A module delivers at most two times its purchase price, price included, then it ends. A Believer's module delivers 220%.

q.q: Can a member withdraw the purchase price of a module?
o: No â€” the price is not refundable and cannot be withdrawn
q.w: The purchase price is not refundable and cannot be withdrawn. Only results and commissions go to the wallet.

q.q: Can a module be cancelled before it reaches 2Ã—?
q.w: A module cannot be cancelled before 2Ã—. It runs until it has delivered two times its price.

q.q: What happens to a module's results on days 1 to 10?
o: Every result auto-rebuys into a small rebuy module with its own 2Ã—
Nothing is paid in the first ten days
q.w: Days 1â€“10: every result auto-rebuys into a new rebuy module, which has its own 2Ã— limit and counts as new volume.

q.q: What appears on day 11?
o: The Auto-Rebuy switch: ON keeps rebuying, OFF sends results to the app wallet
q.w: From day 11 the member's Auto-Rebuy switch decides each day: ON = rebuy, OFF = app wallet.

q.q: What is a Believer?
o: A member who keeps Auto-Rebuy ON for the module's whole life; the module then delivers 220% instead of 200%
A member who never withdraws commission
q.w: The Believer keeps the switch ON for the whole life of the module and the module delivers 220% instead of 200%. The choice is binding until 220%.

q.q: A Believer's 1,000 USDT module ends when it has delivered how much?
q.w: 220% of 1,000 USDT is 2,200 USDT, around day 440 at the average. Not a promise â€” an illustration at the average.

q.q: Is the Believer choice reversible?
o: No â€” the switch stays ON until 220%
q.w: The Believer choice is binding: Auto-Rebuy stays ON until the module has delivered 220%.

q.q: At the engine's average daily result, a 1,000 USDT module's result is aboutâ€¦
q.w: 0.50% of 1,000 USDT is 5 USDT a day â€” at the average. Real days vary from zero to several percent.

q.q: Around which day do a module's results equal its purchase price, at the average?
q.w: At 0.50% a day, results equal the price around day 200 and reach 2Ã— around day 400. Illustrations at the average.

q.q: Does a rebuy module created on days 1â€“10 have its own 2Ã— limit?
o: Yes â€” each rebuy module is a new module with its own 2Ã—
No, it shares the original module's limit
No, rebuy modules have no limit
Only if it is above 1,000 USDT
q.w: Every rebuy module is a module of its own, with its own 2Ã— and counting as new volume for the upline.

q.q: Which sentence about the daily result is right?
o: 0.50% a day is the engine's average; real days vary from zero to several percent and nothing is guaranteed
0.50% is paid every day without exception
The result is fixed by contract at 0.50%
The result can never be below 0.50%
q.w: 0.50% a day is an average over time. Days vary from zero to several percent, the average can change, nothing is guaranteed.

q.q: Founder seats areâ€¦
o: A separate product with their own documents â€” not part of the module or the Momentum Plan
The top rank of the Momentum Plan
q.w: Founder seats are a separate product with their own guide, key facts and FAQ. Point people to those documents or to an agent.

q.q: Of every 100 USDT of trading profit, how much goes to members as their modules' daily results?
q.w: 50 USDT to members, 25 USDT to the compensation plan, 25 USDT to the DAO Treasury.

q.q: Of every 100 USDT of trading profit, how much funds the compensation plan?
q.w: 25 USDT of every 100 USDT of trading profit funds the compensation plan. Every commission comes from here, never from a purchase.

q.q: Of every 100 USDT of trading profit, how much goes to the DAO Treasury?
q.w: 25 USDT of every 100 goes to the DAO Treasury.

q.q: Where does every commission come from?
o: From the compensation plan's share of trading profit â€” never from a purchase
q.w: Commission is paid from the plan's quarter of trading profit, never from anyone's purchase price.

q.q: On a day with no trading profit, what is paid?
o: Nothing â€” no profit, no payout
q.w: No profit, no payout. A day without trading profit pays nobody â€” no results, no commission.

q.q: Commission that no member in a chain qualifies forâ€¦
o: Is split among the members who do qualify
Is paid to the member's sponsor anyway
q.w: Commission no member qualifies for stays with Delta One. It is never redistributed to other members.

q.q: Is 50 / 25 / 25 applied to the purchase price or to trading profit?
q.w: The split applies to trading profit. A purchase price is never shared out to anyone.

q.q: What does a qualified upline receive from a contract on each paid level?
o: 2% of what that contract earns that day
q.w: Two percent of a contract's daily earnings, on every level the rank reaches. Never a share of the purchase price.

q.q: How many levels can the base matrix pay at most?
q.w: Up to 21 levels at Everest; 3 at Fuji, 6 at Kilimanjaro, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21.

q.q: What is the most that base matrix and differential together can ever pay on one contract?
q.w: 21 levels Ã— 2% = 42% of a contract's earnings: base plus differential never exceed it.

q.q: Is the base matrix paid on a member's own module?
o: No â€” it is paid on the contracts in the paid levels below you
q.w: The base matrix is paid on contracts in your paid levels. Your own module pays you its results, not matrix commission.

q.q: Which contracts count for the base matrix?
o: Active modules that earned something that day, inside your paid levels
q.w: Only active modules count, only on days they earn, and only inside the levels your rank reaches.

q.q: A contract earns 50 USDT today. How much does each qualified upline on a paid level receive from it?
q.w: 2% of 50 USDT is 1 USDT â€” per level, per day, from that contract.

q.q: A 10,000 USDT contract at the average earns about 50 USDT a day. Each qualified upline level receives aboutâ€¦
o: 1 USDT a day, about 30 USDT a month
q.w: 2% of 50 USDT is 1 USDT a day, about 30 USDT a month. Small per module â€” rewards come from volume.

q.q: What does the daily cap limit?
o: Base matrix commission per member per day, by rank
q.w: The daily caps (1,000 USDT at Fuji â€¦ 7,000 USDT at Everest) apply to base matrix commission. The differential has no cap.

q.q: What is the daily base-matrix cap at Everest?
q.w: 7,000 USDT a day at Everest; 1,000 at Fuji, 2,000 Kilimanjaro, 3,000 Matterhorn, 4,000 Denali, 5,000 Rainier, 6,000 K-2.

q.q: With 100,000 USDT of modules in your paid levels, at the average, the base matrix pays aboutâ€¦
q.w: 100,000 Ã— 0.50% = 500 USDT of earnings a day; 2% of that is 10 USDT a day, about 300 USDT a month. An illustration at the average.

q.q: Name the seven ranks in order.
o: Fuji, Kilimanjaro, Matterhorn, Denali, Rainier, K-2, Everest
Everest, K-2, Rainier, Denali, Matterhorn, Kilimanjaro, Fuji
Fuji, Matterhorn, Kilimanjaro, Rainier, Denali, K-2, Everest
Fuji, Denali, Kilimanjaro, Matterhorn, Rainier, Everest, K-2
q.w: From the first to the top: Fuji, Kilimanjaro, Matterhorn, Denali, Rainier, K-2, Everest.

q.q: What does Fuji require?
o: Own purchase 1,000 USDT Â· 2 personal enrollees Â· 2,000 USDT qualifying volume
Own purchase 2,500 USDT Â· 3 enrollees Â· 5,000 USDT
Own purchase 1,000 USDT Â· 1 enrollee Â· 1,000 USDT
Own purchase 500 USDT Â· 2 enrollees Â· 2,000 USDT
q.w: Fuji: 1,000 USDT own purchase, 2 personal enrollees, 2,000 USDT of qualifying volume; paid on 3 levels; 6% entitlement; 1,000 USDT daily cap.

q.q: What does Kilimanjaro require?
q.w: Kilimanjaro: 2,500 USDT own purchase, 3 enrollees, 5,000 USDT; levels 1â€“6; 12%; 2,000 USDT daily cap.

q.q: What does Matterhorn require?
q.w: Matterhorn: 6,000 USDT, 4 enrollees, 12,000 USDT; levels 1â€“9; 18%; 3,000 USDT daily cap.

q.q: What does Denali require?
q.w: Denali: 12,000 USDT, 5 enrollees, 25,000 USDT; levels 1â€“12; 24%; 4,000 USDT daily cap.

q.q: What does Rainier require?
q.w: Rainier: 25,000 USDT, 7 enrollees, 75,000 USDT; levels 1â€“15; 30%; 5,000 USDT daily cap.

q.q: What does K-2 require?
q.w: K-2: 50,000 USDT, 12 enrollees, 250,000 USDT; levels 1â€“18; 36%; 6,000 USDT daily cap.

q.q: What does Everest require?
q.w: Everest: 200,000 USDT own purchase, 21 personal enrollees, 1,000,000 USDT of qualifying volume; levels 1â€“21; 42%; 7,000 USDT daily cap.

q.q: How many paid levels does each new rank add?
q.w: Each rank adds three paid levels: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21.

q.q: What is the entitlement at Fuji and at Everest?
q.w: Entitlements: Fuji 6%, Kilimanjaro 12%, Matterhorn 18%, Denali 24%, Rainier 30%, K-2 36%, Everest 42%.

q.q: When are ranks rechecked?
q.w: Ranks are rechecked at every settlement, every day. Only active modules count.

q.q: A module that has reached 2Ã— and endedâ€¦
o: No longer counts for rank or volume
q.w: Only active modules count. A module that has delivered 2Ã— has ended and no longer counts.

q.q: What is the 'own purchase' requirement?
o: The member's own active module (or modules) must reach the rank's amount
The sponsor's module must reach the amount
The whole line must reach the amount
A one-time fee paid to Delta One
q.w: Own purchase is the member's own module(s): 1,000 USDT at Fuji, up to 200,000 USDT at Everest.

q.q: Which three things qualify a rank?
o: Own purchase, personal enrollees, and qualifying volume counted under the line balance rule
Own purchase and time in the plan
Enrollees and the number of levels
q.w: Three steps: your own purchase, your personal enrollees, and your qualifying volume counted line by line.

q.q: What is the daily base-matrix cap at Kilimanjaro?
q.w: Kilimanjaro's daily cap is 2,000 USDT; the caps rise by 1,000 USDT per rank to 7,000 USDT at Everest.

q.q: What is a line?
o: One personal enrollee and everyone beneath them
Every member at the same level
Your own module and its rebuys
q.w: A line is one person you enrolled and everyone beneath them, however deep.

q.q: At Fuji and Kilimanjaro, how much of the qualifying volume can one line count for, at most?
q.w: Half at Fuji and Kilimanjaro: at least two lines are needed.

q.q: At Matterhorn and Denali, how much can one line count for?
q.w: A third at Matterhorn and Denali: at least three lines.

q.q: At Rainier, how much can one line count for?
q.w: A quarter at Rainier: at least four lines.

q.q: At K-2 and Everest, how much can one line count for?
q.w: A fifth at K-2 and Everest: at least five lines.

q.q: A member has 13,500 USDT of volume, 10,000 USDT of it in one line. Which rank can the volume qualify for?
q.w: Matterhorn needs 12,000 USDT with no line above a third (4,000 USDT): the heavy line counts only 4,000, so the counted volume is 7,500 â€” Kilimanjaro, not Matterhorn.

q.q: What happens to volume above a line's share?
o: It does not count toward that rank
q.w: Volume above the share simply does not count. Build wide: more lines, not one tall tower.

q.q: What is the practical lesson of the line balance rule?
o: Build wide â€” several balanced lines, not one heavy line
Build one deep line as fast as possible
Enroll only people who buy big modules
Wait for your downline to balance itself
q.w: Build wide. Several balanced lines qualify; one heavy line is capped at its share.

q.q: Does the line balance rule change how much commission a contract pays?
o: No â€” it decides rank qualification; the contract still pays 2% per paid level
Yes, heavy lines pay less per contract
Yes, balanced lines pay 3% per level
q.w: The rule decides which rank you qualify for. Once qualified, every contract in your paid levels pays the same 2% per level.

q.q: What is the breakage differential?
o: The gap between your rank's entitlement and the highest entitlement already claimed below you in that line, on the same contract
The leftover of the daily cap
q.w: The differential pays leaders the gap between their entitlement (6%â€¦42%) and the highest entitlement already claimed below them in that line.

q.q: Is the breakage differential capped per day?
o: No â€” no cap and no depth limit
Yes, at the rank's daily cap
q.w: The differential has no daily cap and no depth limit. The daily caps apply to the base matrix only.

q.q: A Denali (24%) sits above a Fuji (6%) at the head of a line. What gap does the Denali collect on that line's contracts?
q.w: 24 âˆ’ 6 = 18 points of the contract's earnings, after the base matrix already paid.

q.q: On 1,000,000 USDT of modules in such a line, at the average, 18 points is aboutâ€¦
o: 900 USDT a day, about 27,000 USDT a month
q.w: 1,000,000 Ã— 0.50% = 5,000 USDT of earnings a day; 18% of that is 900 USDT a day, about 27,000 USDT a month. An illustration at the average.

q.q: Why do new lines pay more differential?
o: Nobody below has claimed any of the gap yet, so the first leader collects the whole gap above the line head's entitlement
New lines are exempt from the cap
The base matrix is doubled on new lines
q.w: In a new line where you are the first leader, nothing below you has claimed the gap â€” you collect all of it above the head's entitlement.

q.q: When someone below you reaches your rank, what happens to the gap on their line?
o: Their part of the gap becomes theirs; stay ahead of your leaders to keep it
You both receive the full gap
The gap is paid to Delta One
q.w: Stay ahead: when a leader below you matches your rank, their part of the gap is theirs.

q.q: Base matrix plus differential on one contract can never exceedâ€¦
q.w: Base + differential + whatever is left always equal 42% of the contract's earnings; a member never receives more than the gap to 42%.

q.q: The differential is paid on what?
o: The contract's daily earnings, after the base matrix
q.w: On the contract's daily earnings, on the same days, after the base matrix has been paid.

q.q: Who can earn the breakage differential?
o: Any ranked member whose entitlement is higher than the highest claimed below them in a line
Only the sponsor of the contract's owner
q.w: Any ranked member with a gap above the highest entitlement claimed below them in that line â€” that is how leaders are paid.

q.q: When is settlement?
q.w: Every day at 12:00 UTC. Results and commissions are credited to the app wallet in USDT.

q.q: When does a new module earn its first result?
o: At the settlement after the day the purchase is confirmed
q.w: The first result comes at the settlement after the day the purchase is confirmed.

q.q: What is the minimum withdrawal from the app wallet?
q.w: Withdraw any time, 5 USDT minimum, instant, gas fee only â€” results and commissions, never the purchase price.

q.q: Where are results and commissions credited?
o: To the member's app wallet, in USDT
To a new module automatically, always
q.w: To the app wallet in USDT on BNB Smart Chain (BEP-20). Before day 11, results rebuy; from day 11 the switch decides.

q.q: A member's results on day 11 areâ€¦
o: Withdrawable â€” the first day the result can go to the wallet
q.w: Day 11 is the first day a result can go to the wallet; from day 12 the member's Auto-Rebuy switch decides each day.

q.q: Which word do we use for putting money into a module?
q.w: A module is a purchase. Never deposit, invest, investment, principal or capital.

q.q: Which word do we use for what the engine produces for a module?
q.w: Result â€” never return, ROI, yield, interest or dividend.

q.q: Which word do we use when a result buys a new module?
q.w: Rebuy and Auto-Rebuy â€” never reinvest, compound or roll over.

q.q: Which word do we use for what members earn from the plan?
q.w: Rewards; commission, base matrix, breakage differential. Never passive income, residual, bonus pool or recruitment bonus. Trading profit is what the engine makes.

q.q: Which sentence must go with every conversation about money, results or rewards?
o: Every figure is an illustration at the engine's average daily result; results and rewards are not guaranteed, and most members earn no commission at all
The engine never has a zero day
A module pays every day, no matter what
Returns are guaranteed by the DAO Treasury
q.w: The disclosure line: illustrations at the average; not guaranteed; most members earn no commission at all.

q.q: A prospect asks 'is my money safe?' The right answer isâ€¦
o: Nothing is guaranteed: the price is not refundable and can be lost; only purchase with money you can afford to lose
Yes, the engine has never lost
It is as safe as a bank
q.w: Never promise safety. The purchase price is not refundable and can be lost in whole or in part; only purchase with money you can afford to lose.

q.q: Can you tell a prospect a module pays 0.50% every day?
o: No â€” 0.50% is the average; days vary from zero to several percent and the average can change
Yes, it is the published rate
Yes, if they are a Believer
q.w: 0.50% a day is an average over time, never a daily promise. Say 'average' every time a rate or a date appears.

q.q: Which sentence is wrong?
o: Commission comes from new members' purchases
Commission comes from the plan's quarter of trading profit
Most members earn no commission at all
q.w: Commission never comes from a purchase. It comes from the compensation plan's 25% of trading profit.

q.q: What do you say about the translated documents?
o: They are drafts until a native speaker and compliance have reviewed them; the English edition is the reference
They differ from the English figures
q.w: Translations are drafts pending native-speaker and compliance review; every figure matches the English edition, which is the reference.

q.q: Every document, site and figure of the plan isâ€¦
o: A draft for legal and compliance review, with illustrations at the average
q.w: Draft for legal and compliance review; not legal, tax or financial advice.

q.q: Which rank-day commission figure may you quote to a prospect?
o: One shown in the published documents, always as an illustration at the average with the disclosure
Any figure you have seen a member earn
A figure you work out yourself and round up
The best month of your own upline
q.w: Only published figures, always as illustrations at the average, always with the disclosure. Never quote a figure you cannot show.

q.q: The six rules of the plan areâ€¦
o: Paid on earnings never on purchases Â· no profit no payout Â· balance your lines Â· stay ahead Â· modules end at 2Ã— (only active modules count) Â· paid daily in USDT
Buy big Â· recruit fast Â· one line is enough Â· never withdraw Â· wait for 3Ã— Â· paid monthly
Deposit Â· reinvest Â· guaranteed return Â· residual income Â· bonus pool Â· founder tier
Paid on purchases Â· profit every day Â· one line Â· stay below Â· modules never end Â· paid weekly
q.w: Paid on earnings, never on purchases; no profit, no payout; balance your lines; stay ahead; modules end at 2Ã— and only active modules count; paid daily, in USDT.
